activity.text: 💉 Au Royaume-Uni, le vaccin HPV fait chuter la mortalité à zéro 📊 Une étude de Queen Mary University of London, publiée dans The Lancet, montre que sur la période 2020 à 2024, aucune femme de 20 à 24 ans n’est décédée d’un cancer du col de l’utérus au Royaume-Uni. Dans cette tranche d’âge, près de 90 % avaient été vaccinées vers 12 ans. Sans vaccination, environ 23 décès étaient attendus. 🩺 En Belgique, 641 femmes ont reçu un diagnostic de cancer invasif du col de l’utérus en 2022 et 231 en sont décédées, selon Sciensano. Le remboursement du vaccin a été élargi, mais la sensibilisation reste insuffisante, rappelle aussi All.Can Belgium. Retrouvez notre décryptage complet sur Le journal du Médecin : https://lnkd.in/e-9-PaQ3 ...more ...more
activity.text_en: 💉 In the UK, HPV vaccine drops mortality to zero 📊 A Queen Mary University of London study, published in The Lancet, shows that over the period 2020 to 2024, no women aged 20 to 24 died from cervical cancer in the UK. In this age group, nearly 90% had been vaccinated by age 12. Without vaccination, approximately 23 deaths were expected. 🩺 In Belgium, 641 women were diagnosed with invasive cervical cancer in 2022 and 231 died, according to Sciensano. The reimbursement of the vaccine has been expanded, but awareness remains insufficient, also recalls All.Can Belgium. activity.text: ​Headline: Breakthrough in Neonatology: Can we create an artificial womb? The edge of viability is one of the most challenging frontiers in medicine. Today, I want to highlight an incredible innovation that is moving from research to reality: Artificial Placenta Technology. ​For the smallest premature infants—those born between 22 and 25 weeks—traditional neonatal care, including mechanical ventilation, faces a paradox. While life-saving, it can cause irreversible damage to their underdeveloped lungs and organs. ​The artificial placenta offers a new paradigm: ​💧 It creates a "liquid-filled" environment, mimicking the womb. 🌿 It bypasses the lungs entirely for gas exchange, using an external oxygenator connected via the umbilical cord. 🛡️ It allows a baby’s organs to continue maturing in a protected, fluid state, just as nature intended. ​While still in the trial phase, this technology is a quantum leap for neonatology. It doesn’t just improve survival; it aims to rewrite the long-term health outcomes for our most vulnerable patients. ​As we look to the future of specialized care, this innovation underscores the power of combining deep physiological understanding with advanced bioengineering. ​What other innovations are you watching in the neonatal space? Let's discuss. ​ #Neonatology #MedicalInnovation #Prematurity #Healthcare #ArtificialPlacenta #NICU #FutureOfMedicine ...more ...more

As a parent, I know how much trust we place in pediatricians. That’s why I was thrilled to sit down with Dr. wassim EL BITAR , Head of the Pediatrics Department at CHIREC Hospital Group , for the third episode of our Health Dialogue Series, part of MSD Belgium ’s 60th anniversary celebrations. Our conversation touched on topics that matter deeply to me: ✨ The pivotal role of pediatricians in children's well-being ✨ How they empower (young) parents to make informed healthcare choices ✨ Why prevention is key to building healthier futures ✨ Leveraging AI to tailor communication for diverse communities Dr. El Bitar’s passion for pediatric care is truly inspiring, and I’m grateful for the insights he shared. Thank you, Dr. El Bitar, for your dedication to children’s health and for joining me in this dialogue. ...more ...more

activity.text: As a pediatrician, I was deeply moved by the story of a courageous mother who, after losing her husband to HPV- related cancer, chose to vaccinate both her 11-year-old son and herself against HPV on Christmas Eve 2023. Her determination to raise awareness highlights how essential vaccination is. HPV doesn’t discriminate—it can affect anyone, regardless of gender. Let’s protect our health and that of our loved ones by choosing HPV vaccination together! ...more ...more

💛🏆 Gold Certification Achievement Congratulations to Bellevue Medical Center - Lebanon on achieving Planetree Gold Re-Certification for Excellence in Person-Centered Care! This recognition celebrates Bellevue Medical Center's ongoing commitment to compassionate, person-centered care, where patients, families, and team members are at the heart of every interaction. As one of 157 Planetree Certified organizations, including 101 Gold Certified sites worldwide, Bellevue continues to lead the way in advancing Person-Centered Care. 👏 Congratulations to the entire team on this well-deserved achievement! 🔗 Learn more about the journey to certification: https://ow.ly/xRYv50ZtPOq #Planetree #PersonCenteredCare #PlanetreeCertified #GoldCertification #HealthcareLeadership
Deeply honored by this recognition. Thank you to the Arab Hospitals Federation for highlighting our commitment to excellence and compassionate care🙏🙏

Some hospitals treat person-centered care as a program. Others build it into everything they do. Mr. Nayef Maalouf , President and CEO of Bellevue Medical Center - Lebanon , shared: "At Bellevue Medical Center, excellence is not a goal we pursue occasionally but a standard we uphold in every decision, interaction, and outcome, driven by a core commitment to combine clinical excellence with genuine compassion and create care that truly makes a difference." That's the spirit behind AHF's #GoldInitiativeCertificate : recognizing institutions where clinical excellence and human-centered care aren't competing priorities, but a single, consistent standard. Under Mr. Maalouf's leadership, Bellevue Medical Center became the first hospital in Lebanon to introduce shared medical records, open visitation, and bedside shift reporting, building a person-centered culture recognized by Planetree International, which also honored Mr. Maalouf as its 2023 Caregiver of the Year. At the Arab Hospitals Federation, we are proud to be the platform that brings leaders like Mr. Maalouf and institutions like Bellevue Medical Center into one shared regional standard of excellence. 📅 Stay tuned for the official ceremony information. #AHFExcellenceHasAVoice #GoldInitiative #RoleModelInHealthcareExcellence

The first part of 2026 has been a very enriching period, with the opportunity to present and discuss our work on the application of central and peripheral stimulation techniques in clinical populations across several international meetings. Starting in Krakow (Poland) at the ESPRM - European Society of Physical and Rehabilitation Medicine Congress, followed by OTWorld - International Trade Show & World Congress in Leipzig (Germany), the International Conference on Multiple Sclerosis Fatigue in Siena (Italy), and finally RiMS - Rehabilitation in Multiple Sclerosis in Multiple Sclerosis (RIMS) in Prague (Czech Republic), these events have provided valuable opportunities to exchange ideas with clinicians, researchers, and colleagues from different fields. I am grateful for the stimulating discussions, collaborations, and new perspectives gained throughout these meetings. These exchanges continue to contribute to the development and translation of stimulation-based approaches into clinical practice.
